name: Portfolio Studio
summary: Editorial, type-led portfolio: a giant name that fills the screen with rotating role words, a project index whose pictures follow the pointer (thumbnail cards on phones), an asymmetric six-photo grid with a lightbox, portrait and bio, optional services, and a huge copyable email.

sections.name: header
sections.what: Sticky bar: initial in a circle, the name, Work / About / Contact links, a Say hello button
sections.edit: Usually leave as is. If you remove a section, also remove its nav link

sections.name: hero
sections.what: Meta row (Portfolio + year, Based in city), the name as a giant h1 (fills one line on desktop), a line of rotating role words, an intro sentence, two buttons, a spinning stamp that links to the work
sections.edit: Keep {{business}} as the h1 name. Set the 4 role words to the owner's real roles (the 5th word must repeat the 1st) and update the hidden .sr-only sentence to match. Rewrite the intro in the owner's voice. Keep one h1

sections.name: disciplines
sections.what: Full-bleed accent band with a moving marquee of disciplines
sections.edit: 4 to 8 real disciplines, one or two words each; keep the small star svg after each word

sections.name: index
sections.what: Numbered project index: big-type rows on desktop whose picture follows the pointer; thumbnail cards on phones. Each row links to its picture in the work grid
sections.edit: One row per real project (3 to 8); short real titles and a one or two word category. Keep href=#work-N matching the grid ids. Rewrite the note under the heading

sections.name: work
sections.what: Six photos in an asymmetric editorial grid (shapes a to f: tall, portrait, square, landscape, panorama, tall) with numbered captions, a small call to action, and a lightbox
sections.edit: Keep captions in step with the index titles. To show fewer photos, delete whole figure blocks and their index rows. Rewrite the note under the heading

sections.name: about
sections.what: Portrait with an accent block behind it, a big statement (h2), two bio paragraphs, three small facts (based in, open to, email)
sections.edit: Rewrite the statement and bio in the owner's own words from facts they gave. Never add awards, client names, years or numbers they did not give

sections.name: services
sections.what: Optional list of services with dotted leaders and an Ask for rates email link each (subject = service name)
sections.edit: One item per real service; never invent prices. Remove the whole section if the owner gave no services

sections.name: contact
sections.what: Inverted (dark on light swapped) block: big question, the email as huge type with a Copy email button, phone, city and hours
sections.edit: Rewrite the question if you like. Keep the email link and copy button; remove the hours cell if not relevant

sections.name: footer
sections.what: Copyright with year and name, city, back to top

photo_slots.hint: the owner's strongest piece; a portrait or hero project shot, tall crop
a second project, works in a tall 3:4 crop
a third project or a detail shot, square crop
a panoramic or very wide image (shown 21:9 on desktop)
a friendly portrait of the owner, or the studio at work

behaviors: name scales to fill one line on desktop and shrinks to fit long words on phones
CSS-only rotating role words (screen readers get a plain sentence)
project index: picture follows the pointer on desktop, thumbnail cards on touch screens
lightbox for the work grid (arrows, swipe, Esc)
marquee band, spinning stamp, scroll reveals, sticky glass header, progress bar
quiet custom cursor ring on desktop mouse only (off for touch and reduced motion)
section numbers (01, 02...) are automatic CSS counters, so removing a section renumbers the rest
style_notes: Owns the editorial type-led archetype; colours, fonts, radii and shadows all come from the style kit. Tested with editorial-serif, midnight-neon, neo-brutalist, poster-bold, soft-pastel, minimal-mono and high-contrast-sport at 390 and 1280. Best with editorial-serif, swiss-grid, minimal-mono, newspaper, midnight-neon, dark-luxury.
